Class PythonHttpConversion

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.context.python.PythonHttpConversion
@Internal public final class PythonHttpConversion extends Object
Conversion of Python return values that are HTTP responses or reactive publishers.
Since:
5.2.0

    • convertPublisher

      public static <T,P> @Nullable P convertPublisher(org.graalvm.polyglot.Value value, Class<T> itemType, Class<P> targetType)
      Convert a GraalPy value representing a publisher to the reactive type a method declares: the items are converted to the declared item type and the publisher is then adapted to the declared type (Mono, Flux, a CompletionStage or any reactive type the conversion service knows), so a Python body may return a Flux where the Java signature says Mono, or a Mono where it says CompletableFuture.
      Type Parameters:
      T - The item type
      P - The reactive type
      Parameters:
      value - The source polyglot publisher
      itemType - The declared publisher item type
      targetType - The declared reactive return type
      Returns:
      The converted publisher, or null for None

      Throws:

    • convertReactive

      public static <P> @Nullable P convertReactive(@Nullable Object source, Class<P> targetType)
      Adapt a reactive value (a Publisher or a CompletionStage) to the reactive type a method declares. A value that already is of the declared type is returned as is; a publisher is otherwise wrapped as Mono.from/Flux.from when Reactor is present, completed into a future when a CompletionStage is declared, and converted through the shared ConversionService for any other reactive type; a stage is adapted through the publisher it completes.
      Type Parameters:
      P - The reactive type
      Parameters:
      source - The publisher or completion stage
      targetType - The declared reactive return type
      Returns:
      The adapted value, or null for a null source
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - When the value cannot be adapted to the declared type
